title: Durable queue consumer: retries/backoff + DLQ write path (metrics stubs)
author: Diego Santos
release_notes: Internal: adds durable consumer retry/backoff + DLQ plumbing; exposes initial metrics (stubs) for backlog depth and DLQ volume.
body:
Context: This PR implements the durable queue consumer loop for audit-log-exporter with production-leaning delivery semantics (at-least-once), including retry/backoff, attempt tracking, and a DLQ write path. This is the core worker-side reliability primitive needed before we wire up sink connectors (Splunk/Datadog/S3) and control-plane health reporting. Scope: (1) Consumer reads from the durable queue in batches, (2) processes messages via a handler interface, (3) checkpoints success, (4) retries failures with exponential backoff + jitter, and (5) dead-letters after max attempts with error context preserved. Also includes initial metrics stubs for backlog depth and DLQ depth so SRE dashboards can be unblocked while we finalize queue backend specifics.

Implementation notes: The consumer uses a pluggable Queue interface (Dequeue/Checkpoint/Reschedule/DeadLetter) so we can run the same worker logic across Hosted and Private deployments. Errors are classified as retryable vs non-retryable at the handler boundary (RetryableError wrapper + helper funcs). Retry policy defaults are conservative (initial_backoff=1s, max_backoff=2m, max_attempts=12) and can be configured via env/config. Backoff uses full jitter to avoid retry storms. DLQ records include message_id, destination_id, attempt_count, last_error_class, last_error_message (truncated), and first_seen_at/last_seen_at timestamps; original payload is preserved as-is for replay tooling. Metrics: Added counters/histograms and two gauges that are currently stubbed against the queue implementation (backlog_depth, dlq_depth) to avoid blocking this PR; queue implementations can later populate these accurately.

Example behavior: For a handler error that is retryable, we reschedule with delay=min(max_backoff, initial_backoff*2^(attempt-1)) with jitter. If attempt exceeds max_attempts OR error is explicitly non-retryable, we write to DLQ and checkpoint (ack) the original message to prevent poison-pill loops. Consumer respects context cancellation and will stop fetching new work on shutdown, finishing the in-flight batch.

Test coverage: Unit tests cover retry classification, backoff delay bounds, DLQ transition, and ensuring DLQ write failure does not cause infinite retry loops (we log + increment dlq_write_error_total and keep message unacked so it will reappear; operator action required). Added a small fake queue and fake clock to make backoff deterministic.

Follow-ups: (a) implement queue-backed backlog_depth/dlq_depth gauges once the queue storage is finalized, (b) wire consumer metrics into the shared observability pack dashboards, (c) add runbook guidance for DLQ triage and replay once replay tooling lands, and (d) integrate destination-scoped checkpointing (currently message includes destination_id but consumer does not yet aggregate health per destination).
commits: queue: add consumer loop with batch dequeue + handler dispatch
retries: exponential backoff w/ jitter + attempt tracking
dlq: persist dead-letter record with error context + payload
metrics: add consumer counters/histograms + backlog/dlq gauge stubs
tests: fake queue + backoff/dlq unit tests
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Love the direction. Two asks before approval: (1) please ensure the backoff uses jitter (we've had retry alignment storms before), and (2) clarify what happens if DLQ write fails — we should avoid acking the message if we can't persist it somewhere.

Diego Santos (author): Good call. Added full-jitter backoff (rand in [0, baseDelay]) and documented defaults in config. For DLQ write failure, I changed behavior to NOT checkpoint/ack the message; we log with a stable error code and increment dlq_write_error_total so ops can see it. This means the message will be retried later, but we avoid losing it.

Sean Gallagher (review): Requesting one change: the consumer loop currently polls immediately when queue is empty; can we add a small idle sleep (or block on Dequeue) to avoid hot looping in low traffic? Also +1 to context cancellation handling.

Diego Santos (author): Updated: Dequeue now supports a wait timeout (long-poll style) in the interface; fake queue implements it; consumer backs off to 250ms idle sleep when empty if implementation returns quickly. Also added a unit test to ensure we honor ctx.Done().

Allison Grant (review): Metrics look fine. Can we standardize names/labels to match our conventions? Specifically: use destination_type and destination_id labels sparingly; cardinality concerns. I'd suggest destination_type only for now, and keep destination_id in logs only.

Diego Santos (author): Agreed. Changed metrics to label by destination_type only; destination_id is logged (structured) on error paths. backlog_depth/dlq_depth are global gauges for now; once the queue backend supports per-destination depth we'll revisit (likely sampled / top-N).
Ethan Park (review): Approved after latest push. Thanks for tightening DLQ semantics.
Sean Gallagher (review): Approved. Please link this PR in ENG-13923 and note the DLQ write failure behavior in the runbook follow-up.
Diego Santos (author): Linked in ENG-13923 and added a TODO in README/runbook section for DLQ failure behavior.
